reports.name: Strategy

snapshot.holdings: 850,849 BTC (~4.05% of 21M max supply), acquired for ~$64.20B aggregate, avg cost $75,452/BTC

reports.email_summary: MSCI confirmed MSTR's index removal while BTC purchases slowed and the treasury swung back to a ~$9.6B paper loss.
reports.bottom_line: The confirmed MSCI deletion removes a passive-demand pillar just as Strategy's weekly BTC buying pace collapsed (1,036 BTC then only 485 BTC) and a greater share of ATM proceeds went to defending STRC's par value rather than accumulating bitcoin. With BTC near $64K versus a $75,452 average cost basis, the treasury has flipped back into a large unrealized loss, reinforcing the bearish setup for the financing flywheel.
source_conflicts: mNAV estimates diverge sharply across sources for mid-November 2026: mnav.com shows ~1.20x (Nov 15), a macro research note cites 1.09x (Nov 15-16), while another tracker showed a 0.87x discount in early November — likely reflecting different calculation methods (basic vs. enterprise-adjusted) and intraday price swings; no single reliable mNAV figure can be confirmed for this snapshot.

Total BTC holdings as of Nov 8 are reported as both 850,364 (Investing.com, mnav.com) and figures citing slightly different average costs; as of Nov 15 holdings are consistently reported at 850,849 BTC across multiple sources.

updates.headline: MSCI confirms Strategy removal from USA Index Nov 30
updates.what_happened: MSCI published its November index review confirming Strategy will be deleted from the MSCI USA Index and other global equity benchmarks at the close of November 30, under a new rule excluding 'non-operating' asset-holding companies. Strategy had argued in prior letters that exclusion would have no meaningful business impact, but analysts estimate billions in passive-fund outflows as index trackers are forced to sell.
updates.thesis_fit: Loss of passive index demand could compress the mNAV premium further and make equity-based financing for BTC purchases more expensive or less available, directly threatening the capital-markets flywheel the thesis depends on.

updates.headline: Strategy buys 1,036 BTC, STRC buyback outpaces purchase
updates.what_happened: For the week of Nov 2-8, Strategy sold 2,051,348 MSTR shares for $283.8 million net proceeds, using $81.9 million to buy 1,036 BTC at an average $79,012/BTC, while $188.3 million went to repurchasing STRC preferred stock. Total holdings reached 850,364 BTC.
updates.thesis_fit: BTC accumulation continued but the majority of new ATM-dilution proceeds funded preferred buybacks rather than bitcoin purchases, muting BTC-per-share accretion from this raise.

updates.headline: BTC buying pace drops 59% to just 485 coins
updates.what_happened: For the week of Nov 9-15, Strategy sold 2,087,040 MSTR shares for $244.7 million, but allocated only $33.4 million (14%) to buy 485 BTC at $68,887/BTC — a sharp pullback from the prior week's 1,036 BTC. The bulk, $206.3-228.1 million (84%), funded STRC preferred-stock repurchases. Holdings rose to 850,849 BTC at an average cost of $75,452.
updates.thesis_fit: A shrinking share of dilutive capital raises is going toward BTC accumulation versus preferred-stock price defense, which weakens the bitcoin-per-share growth argument at the core of the thesis.

updates.headline: BTC treasury swings back to ~$9.6B unrealized loss
updates.what_happened: With bitcoin trading near $64,000-68,000 against Strategy's $75,452 average acquisition cost, the company's bitcoin position is now carrying an estimated $9.6-9.8 billion paper loss, reversing the previously reported multi-billion-dollar unrealized gain from earlier in the fall.
updates.thesis_fit: Under fair-value accounting this swing drives large non-cash GAAP volatility and signals that a sustained BTC price slide below the average cost basis pressures both reported earnings and the equity's mNAV, reinforcing the discount risk to the financing flywheel.

reports.name: Metaplanet

snapshot.holdings: 44,000 BTC (as of September 30, 2026; confirmed on company site as of November 12, 2026)

reports.email_summary: Metaplanet slashed FY2026 guidance after a ¥27B loss, and MSCI confirmed its Nov 30 index removal, even as buybacks continue.
reports.bottom_line: This week brought a confirmed negative catalyst (MSCI exclusion effective Nov 30) layered onto a steep guidance cut and nine-month net loss tied to BTC valuation/sale losses and mNAV-constrained financing. Ongoing buybacks below mNAV are a partial offset, but BTC accumulation has effectively stalled while the stock trades near 0.49x-0.72x mNAV.
source_conflicts: mNAV estimates diverge depending on methodology: cryptoticker.io calculated 0.72x using enterprise value versus 0.49x using market capitalization, both as of November 12, 2026.
Buyback utilization percentages are reported inconsistently across outlets (54.4% of share count vs. 47.1% of yen budget), reflecting the two different caps (200M shares / ¥60B) in the same program.

updates.headline: Metaplanet slashes FY2026 revenue, profit guidance 59-74%
updates.what_happened: Metaplanet cut its FY2026 revenue forecast from ¥16 billion to ¥6.5 billion and operating profit from ¥11.4 billion to ¥3 billion. The company posted a nine-month net loss of ¥27.16 billion (~$170 million) versus a ¥13.53 billion profit a year earlier, driven by Bitcoin valuation and sale losses, and explicitly linked the slowdown to capping financing while its share price traded below 1.0x mNAV.
updates.thesis_fit: Directly confirms the thesis-weakening scenario of financing constraints and slowed, less-accretive BTC accumulation when mNAV is below 1.0x.

updates.headline: MSCI confirms Metaplanet removal from Japan Small Cap Index
updates.what_happened: MSCI's November 2026 Index Review formally listed Metaplanet for deletion from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index, with the change taking effect after the close of trading on November 30, 2026. This converts the prior 'under review' exclusion risk into a confirmed, dated event that will trigger passive-fund selling.
updates.thesis_fit: Confirmed index exclusion removes a passive-flow support and validates the governance/mNAV concerns that drove MSCI's review, directly relevant to the MSCI checklist item.

updates.headline: Buyback continues: 108.7M shares repurchased, ~54% of cap used
updates.what_happened: Metaplanet disclosed it repurchased an additional 12,256,200 shares for about ¥3.0 billion between November 1-12, bringing cumulative repurchases since the October 14 program start to 108.7 million shares for ¥28.27 billion. This represents 54.4% of the 200-million-share limit and 47.1% of the ¥60 billion budget under the authorization running through October 2027.
updates.thesis_fit: Executed (not merely authorized) buybacks while shares trade below mNAV directly raises BTC-per-share for remaining holders, consistent with the thesis's most important accretive-action checklist item.

updates.headline: Superplanet names CIO, plans US perpetual preferred issuance
updates.what_happened: Super League Enterprise (soon to be renamed Superplanet upon closing Metaplanet's 2,100 BTC contribution) announced Jesse Myers will join as incoming Chief Investment Officer. The release stated Superplanet intends to pursue perpetual preferred equity issuance post-closing to run an 'Amplified Bitcoin' strategy aimed at growing Bitcoin per common share.
updates.thesis_fit: This is a subsidiary-level (Nasdaq-listed Superplanet) capital-structure plan rather than a direct Metaplanet TSE share action, but it signals management's continued preference for preferred/debt financing over common dilution, which aligns with the thesis's preferred financing checklist item.

reports.name: Asset Entities / Strive
reports.email_summary: Strive keeps buying BTC at a loss to spot while raising preferred dividend costs and shares sink 10% in a crypto selloff.
reports.bottom_line: Strive's weekly BTC accumulation continues but recent purchases are now underwater versus spot, cash is shrinking, and the preferred dividend rate just rose, adding cost pressure even as some institutional holders added shares. Net effect is modestly negative for the near-term execution story, though the long-term accumulation thesis remains intact.
source_conflicts: Market cap (~$2.72B) cited in same-day coverage predates the ~10% premarket share price decline on Nov 16, so market cap/mNAV figures from that day are inconsistent depending on timing.
Cash balance change ($22.3M decline to $465.3M) was not explicitly tied to the $17.5M BTC purchase or the $10M preferred raise in the 8-K, per secondary reporting.

updates.headline: Strive buys 251 BTC at a loss to current spot price
updates.what_happened: Strive's Form 8-K disclosed the purchase of 251 bitcoin between Nov. 7-13 at an average cost of $69,853 per coin, bringing total holdings to 43,404 BTC. The filing also showed cash fell $22.3 million to $465.3 million and that Strive raised about $10 million by selling 104,478 shares of its 15% fixed-rate Series A (SATS) preferred stock, with no common or variable-rate SATA shares sold during the week.
updates.thesis_fit: Continued BTC accumulation supports the treasury thesis, but buying at $69,853 while bitcoin traded near $64,300-$68,800 means this tranche sits at an unrealized loss, and funding it via expensive 15% fixed preferred raises the cost-of-capital bar for a durable BTC-per-share story.

updates.headline: Strive raises SATA preferred dividend rate to 13.25%
updates.what_happened: Strive's board increased the dividend rate on its Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock (SATA) from 13.00% to 13.25% per annum, effective for periods starting December 1, 2026, per an 8-K filing.
updates.thesis_fit: A higher preferred dividend rate increases the cash yield Strive must cover from its 18-month reserve and operating cash flow, adding to the capital-structure cost that bears on durability of the BTC-per-share strategy.

updates.headline: BNY Mellon, State Street raise ASST stakes in Q3 13Fs
updates.what_happened: A Nov. 5 13F showed Bank of New York Mellon raised its Strive stake 28% to 237,100 shares worth $6.97 million as of Sept. 30. A separate Nov. 12 13F showed State Street raised its Strive position 12% to roughly $50 million.
updates.thesis_fit: Incremental institutional buying during Q3 is a modest positive signal for market trust in the treasury story, partially offsetting the recently reported reduction in Fidelity's passive stake.

reports.name: BitMine Immersion

snapshot.holdings: 6,077,745 ETH (~4.97% of ETH supply) + 216 BTC + $180M Beast Industries stake + $67M Eightco stake; total crypto/cash/"moonshots" ~$11.8B as of Nov 15, 2026

reports.email_summary: BitMine keeps buying ETH weekly as holdings value falls to $11.8B on price decline; MSCI spared BMNR while Strategy got cut.
reports.bottom_line: BitMine continued disciplined weekly ETH accumulation and avoided the MSCI index-exclusion fate that hit Strategy, but total treasury value fell sharply on ETH price weakness and the staked-ETH ratio has stagnated for three straight weeks. A new retail-voting program that defaults shares to Board recommendations is a mild governance watch-item given the company's history of large share-authorization asks.

updates.headline: BitMine adds 7,653 ETH as holdings value falls to $11.8B
updates.what_happened: BitMine's weekly 8-K disclosed ETH holdings of 6,077,745 tokens (4.97% of supply) as of Nov 15, up 7,653 ETH for the week, but total crypto/cash/moonshots value fell to $11.8 billion from $14.5 billion earlier in the month as ETH's price dropped to $1,823. Staked ETH held flat at 5,227,037 for a third straight week, meaning the staking ratio slipped to about 86% of holdings even as token count grew. Chairman Tom Lee called the ETH decline a "waterfall decline in price" that he attributes to Nvidia-related margin selling in Asia and investors raising cash ahead of the Anthropic IPO.
updates.thesis_fit: Continued weekly accumulation discipline is thesis-supportive, but a stagnant staking balance alongside growing token count and a sharp mark-to-market value decline are mild negatives for the custody/staking-economics and ETH-per-share legs of the thesis.

updates.headline: MSCI removes Strategy from indexes; BitMine not named
updates.what_happened: In its November 2026 Index Review, MSCI confirmed removal of Strategy's Class A shares from its USA Large Cap Index and Global Investable Market Indexes effective after the Nov. 30 close, under new rules targeting non-operating, crypto-heavy balance sheets. BitMine was not named among the companies removed, and BMNR shares rose on the news even as Strategy shares lagged.
updates.thesis_fit: Avoiding MSCI exclusion removes a near-term passive-selling overhang that is now weighing on peer treasury vehicles, a direct positive for BitMine's index-related positioning.

updates.headline: BitMine launches retail voting program defaulting to Board
updates.what_happened: BitMine filed a DEFA14A introducing a "Retail Voting Program" that lets shareholders opt in to have their shares automatically voted in line with Board recommendations at future meetings, modeled on similar programs at large-cap companies. Shareholders retain the ability to override individual votes or opt out, but the program is designed to raise support for future proposals without issuing new shares to secure quorum.
updates.thesis_fit: Given BitMine's history of large share-authorization requests to fund its ETH strategy, a program that streamlines Board-aligned voting is a governance item worth monitoring for how it affects shareholder scrutiny of future dilutive financing proposals.

sector.bottom_line: MSCI's November review confirmed removal of Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi from its global indexes (effective Nov 30) while sparing Ethereum-treasury SharpLink, even as a hawkish Fed pivot toward serial 2027 rate hikes further tightens financing conditions for the beaten-down treasury-company sector.

updates.headline: MSCI confirms Strategy, Metaplanet, Upexi index deletions
updates.what_happened: MSCI's November index review, published Nov 11, listed Strategy for deletion from the MSCI USA Index and Metaplanet from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index, effective at the close of trading Nov 30, with crypto treasury firm Upexi also removed. Ethereum treasury company SharpLink was not included among the deletions in the review and instead remains on a watchlist under the same non-operating-company framework.

updates.headline: White House nominates four SEC, CFTC commissioner picks
updates.what_happened: The White House nominated Kristin N. Johnson and Steven Levine for SEC commissioner seats and Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland for CFTC seats, filling vacancies at both crypto-relevant regulators. The Senate Agriculture Committee will consider the CFTC nominees while Senate Banking handles the SEC picks, with a confirmation hearing already set for November 19.

updates.headline: Fed officials signal December hike, more tightening into 2027
updates.what_happened: Federal Reserve officials delivered hawkish remarks this week that solidified market expectations for a 25-basis-point December rate hike, with futures now pricing consecutive quarter-point increases in December, January and March 2027 rather than just December and March as previously expected. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said on Nov 13 that officials will "need to, in all likelihood, raise rates," citing persistent inflation and stronger-than-expected wholesale and consumer price data.
